test: seven candidate explanations for the LINCS gene x line interaction, one shared harness

candidates.hypothesis: Landmark volatility is a property of the cell line — some landmarks are intrinsically more reactive in some lines regardless of what was knocked down — so weighting each landmark by its line-specific responsiveness (measured from other genes' knockdowns in that line) should reconstruct the gene x line interaction.
candidates.coverage: 9/9 lines (PC3 MCF7 VCAP A375 HA1E A549 HT29 HEPG2 HCC515), all 978 landmarks, all 3801 genes. The volatility statistics are computed from LINCS itself, so there is no external-source coverage gap and nothing was imputed. The three expression columns (shared with the baseline) cover 949/978 landmarks and 3629/3801 genes; the missing ones are set to 0 exactly as H.expression_baseline does. Per-line n: PC3 3801, MCF7 3687, VCAP 3741, A375 3694, HA1E 3801, A549 3724, HT29 3665, HEPG2 3562, HCC515 3522.
candidates.notes:
NULL RESULT. Arm 0.0034 vs same-session H.expression_baseline 0.0033; paired delta +0.0001 +/- 0.0003, t=0.16. Against the 0.2487 construct ceiling the arm explains 1.4% — i.e. nothing beyond the expression baseline it contains.

LEAK CONTROL (the load-bearing design choice). Every per-(landmark, line) statistic comes from a DISJOINT HALF of the genes: genes are split into half 0/half 1 by a stable md5 hash of the symbol (same split in every line), and a query for gene g reads only statistics built from the half g is NOT in. So g's own knockdown never enters any number it is scored against, in any line. I deliberately did NOT use leave-one-out: the harness residual is mean-zero across genes within a line (verified, column mean 0.0005 vs sd 0.54), so LOO-mean equals -R[i]/(n-1) EXACTLY — a sign-flipped copy of the target — and LOO-variance carries -R[i]^2/(n-1). Either would have manufactured a large fake score. The half-split has no algebraic path back to the held-out row. One residual contamination is inherent to the harness and unavoidable: its line-mean subtraction averages over all genes including the scored one, a 1/3800-level effect I did not try to remove.

THE ARM NESTS THE BASELINE. Feature columns 3,4,6 reproduce H.expression_baseline exactly (landmark expression, knocked-down gene's expression, their product); columns 0,1,2,5,7 add half-split landmark SD, line-specific excess volatility, mean|response|, and their products with gene expression. So the +0.0001 delta is precisely the value added by landmark responsiveness, and it is zero.

THE PREMISE IS TRUE — THE MECHANISM STILL CANNOT WORK. This is not a measurement failure. The volatility profile is measured almost perfectly (within-line half-split reliability 0.986) and is genuinely line-specific (cross-line correlation of volatility profiles only 0.545, min 0.425, max 0.670). Landmarks really are differentially reactive by line. The problem is structural, and I measured it before scoring: any feature depending only on (landmark, line) predicts the same profile for every gene in a line, and the residual is mean-zero across genes within a line by construction, so those correlations cancel. The BEST POSSIBLE gene-independent within-line profile (PC1 of the other half's residuals) scores mean r of only +0.0027 (PC3), +0.0135 (MCF7), +0.0137 (HT29) while its mean |r| is 0.23, 0.20, 0.26. The magnitude alignment is large and real; the signs cancel. Landmark volatility tells you HOW BIG the response at a landmark will be, never in WHICH DIRECTION, and the interaction target is signed. Any future arm built on line-level landmark statistics alone is capped near zero a priori.

NO CONSISTENCY ACROSS LINES. The arm beats the baseline in only 4/9 lines, and essentially the entire positive delta comes from one line: A549 (arm +0.0114 vs base +0.0029). The arm is WORSE than baseline in PC3 (+0.0031 vs +0.0046), MCF7 (+0.0015 vs +0.0047), VCAP (+0.0006 vs +0.0029) and A375 (+0.0008 vs +0.0028). Median pair correlation 0.0052, frac>0 0.526.

PROTOCOL. 2 of the 3 allowed H.evaluate runs used (baseline, arm), both max_train_per_line=300, both in the same session and same process, both returning n=33197 in identical pair order so the paired test is valid. No features were tuned after seeing a score — the feature set was fixed before the first evaluate call, and I did not spend the third run trying to rescue the result. Baseline came in at 0.0033 here vs the 0.0029 quoted in the brief; I report the same-session number for the like-for-like comparison. Harness and colab/ untouched; scratch code in scratchpad/wf/lmresp.py and scratchpad/wf/run.py.

candidates.hypothesis: The gene x line interaction is driven by line-specific fitness dependency — knocking down a gene the line actually relies on (low CRISPR gene effect in that line) should propagate broadly, while knocking down a dispensable gene should not — so line-specific essentiality of the knocked-down gene, of each landmark, and their product should predict the residual.
candidates.coverage: Full coverage on all three axes. Lines: 9/9 (every LINCS line maps to a DepMap ModelID present in gene_effect.npz, including HA1E = ACH-001310). Knocked-down genes: 3566/3801 (93.8%) have a real gene-effect value; the other 235 fall back to 0 in the two gene-level columns. Landmarks: 937/978 (95.8%) present in the CRISPR gene list; the 41 missing are zeroed and masked, not imputed. Raw NaN rate inside the 9x17916 slice was 0.40%, filled with that gene's mean across the 9 lines (all-NaN genes zeroed and masked).
candidates.notes:
Null, and slightly worse than the reference. Arm 0.00128 vs H.expression_baseline 0.00331 run in the same session and same settings (max_train_per_line=300, lam=1e-2, identical 33,197 scored pairs): paired delta -0.00203, se 0.00062, t=-3.26. The baseline reproduced at 0.00331 against the quoted 0.0029, so the comparison is like-for-like. Against the 0.2487 disjoint-construct ceiling the arm reaches 0.5%. It is technically distinguishable from zero (t=3.60 vs 0) but so is the baseline (t=6.12), and neither is biologically meaningful at this scale.

Features (6 columns, no tuning, single design, evaluated once): landmark gene-effect in this line; landmark gene-effect z-scored across the 9 lines; knocked-down gene's gene-effect in this line; its z-score across the 9 lines; and the two interactions (landmark_raw x kd_raw, landmark_z x kd_z). Exactly 2 H.evaluate calls were used, no feature iteration.

Likely reason it fails, measured rather than assumed: DepMap gene effect is overwhelmingly a gene main effect, not a gene x line quantity. Across the 9 lines, mean pairwise correlation of whole gene-effect profiles is 0.860, and only 12.5% of gene-effect variance is between-line. The harness target has already had the gene main effect removed, so the part of essentiality that survives the residualization is the small 12.5% differential component, which carries little information about a knockdown's 978-dim transcriptional direction.

Structural caveat, inherent to the metric and shared with the baseline: the two gene-level columns are constant across landmarks within a pair, so they cannot move a within-pair Pearson correlation on their own; all predictive work has to come from the landmark-varying columns and the two interaction terms. This is the same shape as H.expression_baseline, so it does not bias the comparison, but it means the hypothesis is really being tested through its interaction terms.

candidates.hypothesis: A knockdown is buffered in a cell line where the gene's paralogue is well expressed there, so the same shRNA produces a weaker/different transcriptional response in that line — making paralogue expression context a source of the gene x line interaction.
candidates.coverage: All 9 lines covered (every LINCS line maps to a DepMap expression profile via lincs/line_map.json; 9/9). Gene coverage is the limit: of 3,801 knocked-down genes, 3,617 appear in para/paralogs.tsv, 3,012 have >=1 paralogue, and 3,008 have >=1 paralogue that is measured in depmap_expr_aligned.npz — 79.1% of genes, covering 26,273 / 33,197 (gene,line) pairs. Median 7 measured paralogues among covered genes. The remaining 793 genes are singletons or absent from the table; I did NOT impute a paralogue for them — they get an explicit has_paralogue=0 indicator and zeroed paralogue columns so all 33,197 pairs stay scorable and the comparison to the baseline is on identical pairs. The covered-only subset is reported separately below.
candidates.notes:
RESULT. Paralogue arm 0.0008 vs H.expression_baseline 0.0033 in the same session (same process, both max_train_per_line=300): delta -0.0025, se 0.0007, paired t -3.73. On the covered subset only (n=26,273 pairs whose gene has a measured paralogue): arm 0.0011 vs base 0.0040, delta -0.0028, t -3.49. Per-line arm scores straddle zero (PC3 +0.0028, MCF7 +0.0038, HT29 +0.0024, HCC515 +0.0007, HEPG2 -0.0005, A549 -0.0006, HA1E -0.0012, VCAP -0.0015, A375 +0.0013). Features were 11 columns: landmark expression z in this line, plus paralogue max / mean / identity-weighted-mean expression (z across the 9 lines), log paralogue count, has-paralogue indicator, and each of those crossed with landmark expression. Against the 0.2487 construct ceiling this is nothing.

SUPERSET CONTROL (3rd and last evaluate run). My arm is not a strict superset of the baseline — it omits the baseline's gz and lm*gz terms — so a deficit vs baseline is partly just the missing gz. I therefore ran baseline columns + paralogue columns (13 cols): 0.00065 vs baseline 0.0033, delta -0.00267, t -4.61 (covered-only delta -0.00325, t -4.50). Adding paralogue features on top of the baseline makes held-out prediction significantly WORSE, not merely no better. At fixed ridge lam the 10 extra columns are pure variance. So the null is not "underpowered" — paralogue context carries no usable signal about this interaction and actively costs.

SIGN (you asked, and told me not to assume). Direct test on the harness residual, no model fitting: correlation between max paralogue expression in the line and the L2 magnitude of that pair's interaction residual, with magnitude z-scored within held-out line. Pooled over covered pairs: r = -0.0199 (pmax), -0.0050 (pmean), n=26,273. Within-gene across lines — the actual buffering claim, free of gene-level confounds — mean r = -0.0151, median -0.0070, n=3,006 genes, t = -2.30. The sign is NEGATIVE, i.e. the BUFFERING direction (paralogue well expressed here -> weaker response here), which is the OPPOSITE sign to what loops 239-240 got on DepMap fitness. But it is nominally significant only because n=3,006, and r=-0.015 is ~0.02% of the variance in response magnitude. I would not call this a real effect; I would call it the sign you get when the effect is zero and the estimator has 3,000 samples.

WHY THE SIGN TEST AND THE HARNESS DISAGREE IN KIND — the caveat that matters most for interpreting this arm. H.evaluate scores Pearson correlation per (gene,line) pair, which is invariant to the overall amplitude of the response vector. Buffering in its pure form is an AMPLITUDE effect: the same transcriptional response, scaled down. Such an effect is invisible to this metric by construction. So this arm can only detect paralogue effects that change the DIRECTION/SHAPE of the response, not its size. My reading: the weak buffering-signed magnitude effect above is the only thing paralogues do here, and the harness cannot and should not credit it. If anyone wants to chase paralogue buffering further, the target has to be response magnitude, not the correlation the harness scores — and even then the ceiling on that magnitude signal looks like r ~ -0.015.

candidates.hypothesis: Recurrent activating hotspot mutations (KRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA-class gain-of-function alleles) rewire signalling so that a knockdown's downstream consequences depend on which oncogenic driver is active in the line — predicted from the knocked-down gene's hotspot status, each landmark's hotspot status, the line's hotspot burden, and their interactions.
candidates.coverage: All 9/9 LINCS lines are present in OmicsSomaticMutationsMatrixHotspot.csv (via lincs/line_map.json) — no imputation needed. But the informative content is tiny. Of 542 hotspot-matrix genes, only 15 vary across the 9 lines: APC, BCOR, BRAF, C12orf4, CDKN2A, KEAP1, KRAS, NBN, NRAS, PIK3CA, PREX2, SMAD4, STK11, TERT, TP53. Zero genes are hotspot in all 9. Per-line hotspot burden: PC3 0, HA1E 0, VCAP 1, A375 2, MCF7 3, A549 3, HCC515 3, HT29 4, HEPG2 4 — 20 nonzero cells in a 9x15 grid. 55/978 landmarks appear in the matrix at all and only 6/978 have hotspot status that VARIES across the 9 lines (TERT, PIK3CA, TP53, NRAS, CDKN2A, KEAP1). Only 11/3801 knocked-down genes are varying-hotspot genes, covering 99/33197 (gene,line) pairs. Features were emitted for every pair, so all 33,197 pairs were scored in both arms; 0 NaNs.
candidates.notes:
Clean null, and worse than the reference. Mean held-out r = -0.0000846 vs H.expression_baseline 0.0033150 run in the same session on the identical 33,197 pairs (max_train_per_line=300, lam=1e-2 default). Paired delta -0.0034, SE 0.00057, t = -5.98 — the hotspot arm is significantly BELOW the already-negligible expression baseline, i.e. it is indistinguishable from zero against a ceiling of 0.2487.

YOU ASKED ME TO FLAG IF FEWER THAN ~20 HOTSPOT GENES VARY: only 15 do, so yes, the hypothesis is carried by a handful of features — and in practice by even fewer than that. Only 6 of 978 landmarks have varying hotspot status, so the landmark-level feature vector is 972/978 zeros and is driven by 6 columns.

The structural reason this cannot work, which I think matters more than the number: for a given held-out line, the only landmark-varying features available are the line's hotspot vector and static landmark priors. The knocked-down gene's hotspot status and the line's burden are scalars broadcast across landmarks, so after the harness's intercept and pear()'s centering they contribute nothing to within-profile correlation, and the burden interaction only rescales the same vector (correlation is scale-invariant). The consequence is that within a held-out line essentially every knocked-down gene receives the SAME predicted shape up to sign and scale — differing only for the 99/33197 pairs whose KD gene is itself hotspot-mutant. A single fixed per-line direction is precisely the line main effect, which the harness residual has already subtracted, so this arm is structurally incapable of expressing gene x line interaction. That is a property of the data, not of my feature coding.

Per-line means (mine vs baseline) are uniformly at noise: PC3 +0.00074/+0.00458, MCF7 -0.00056/+0.00471, VCAP +0.00005/+0.00294, A375 -0.00081/+0.00280, HA1E -0.00059/+0.00170, A549 +0.00032/+0.00295, HT29 +0.00066/+0.00386, HEPG2 -0.00070/+0.00329, HCC515 +0.00010/+0.00302. Sign flips across lines with no pattern. PC3 and HA1E carry zero hotspot mutations in this matrix (HA1E is immortalised normal kidney epithelium; PC3's TP53 loss is a frameshift, not a hotspot), so for those two held-out lines the entire hotspot-dosage feature block is identically zero and the arm falls back to line-invariant landmark priors.

Post-hoc subgroup, reported for completeness and not as a finding: the 99 pairs whose knocked-down gene is itself a varying-hotspot gene scored -0.00306 vs -0.00008 for the other 33,098 — if anything worse, n far too small to mean anything.

I did not tune. Two H.evaluate calls total (my arm, then the baseline); no feature variants were tried and nothing was re-run after seeing a score. Caveat on the gain-of-function framing: DepMap's hotspot call is a recurrence-based annotation, not a functional one, and it is binary/dosage-coded, so it carries no information about which pathway is activated or how strongly — a hypothesis that hotspots differ "in kind" from damaging mutations is not really testable with this encoding alone. candidates.hypothesis: A knockdown's landmark response should shift when the pathway it feeds is already broken by a damaging mutation in that line — but damaging mutations are too rare in these 9 lines to define any per-(gene,line) direction, and the feature form they permit is exactly the per-line mean the residual already removes.
candidates.coverage: All 9/9 lines present in OmicsSomaticMutationsMatrixDamaging.csv (PC3 MCF7 VCAP A375 HA1E A549 HT29 HEPG2 HCC515, all matched via lincs/line_map.json; no imputation). Landmarks: 873/978 map into the 19,097-gene damaging matrix. But damage is extremely sparse: damaged genes per line = PC3 12, MCF7 30, VCAP 13, A375 54, HA1E 17, A549 63, HT29 41, HEPG2 18, HCC515 172; intersecting with the 978 landmarks leaves only 1-6 damaged landmarks per line (PC3 2, MCF7 1, VCAP 2, A375 2, HA1E 1, A549 3, HT29 5, HEPG2 3, HCC515 6). Knocked-down genes: 3381/3801 present in the matrix (the missing 420 treated as undamaged, not dropped); only 83 of 30,429 (gene,line) combos have the knocked-down gene itself damaged (0.27%). Hotspot matrix covers only 542 genes, 55/978 landmarks, 0-4 hotspot genes per line. All 33,197 held-out pairs scored, 33,197 finite, no pairs skipped.
candidates.notes:
Ran H.evaluate 3x in one session, max_train_per_line=300. Baseline H.expression_baseline scored 0.003315 in this same session (slightly above the quoted 0.0029 because that reference used the default max_train_per_line=500; the like-for-like comparison is against 0.003315). Arm A = the requested feature set exactly (k=4: landmark damaged in line, knocked-down gene damaged in line, line damaged-gene burden, and their interaction) scored -0.000369, delta -0.003684, paired t=-6.52. Both arms land at zero and are significantly BELOW the expression baseline, i.e. the mutation features carry no usable signal and their ridge fit slightly displaces the intercept.

Structural defect worth recording, because it makes this null near-forced rather than merely empirical: two of the four requested features (knocked-down gene's damage status, line burden) are constant across landmarks within a pair, so they contribute only a per-pair offset and cannot move a within-pair Pearson correlation at all. That leaves the prediction for every pair in a held-out line as (a + b*dmg_kd) * DLM_line + const — the same 978-vector up to sign and scale for all ~3700 genes in that line. A fixed per-line direction is precisely what residuals() already subtracts as the line mean, so its mean correlation is ~0 by construction. The only thing that could break the degeneracy is the sign flip when the knocked-down gene is itself damaged, and that fires on 83/30,429 combos. So this arm could not have expressed a gene x line interaction even if one existed in the mutation data.

To separate "hypothesis is wrong" from "feature form is degenerate", I pre-registered and report one extension (Arm B, k=12) adding a genuinely 3-way term: BioGRID physical-neighbour damage load per landmark (dense — 94-594 landmarks per line have a damaged partner, vs 1-6 damaged directly), whether each landmark is a physical partner of the knocked-down gene, and the partner x damage interactions. Arm B scored -0.000229, delta -0.003544, t=-6.16. Also null. So the null survives giving the "pathway is already broken" reading its denser, non-separable operationalization; it is not purely an artifact of the sparse literal encoding.

Caveats on how to read this: (1) damaging-mutation calls are near-binary and near-absent at landmark resolution in these 9 lines, so this is a low-power test of the pathway idea, not a decisive refutation — a mutation source with broader per-line coverage, or a mutation-to-pathway mapping over curated gene sets rather than BioGRID degree, would be a different test; (2) HA1E is an immortalized normal line and HCC515 carries 172 damaged genes (14x HA1E), so burden is heavily confounded with lineage/MSI status, but burden is a per-pair constant here and therefore inert regardless; (3) no tuning — Arm A is the requested spec verbatim, Arm B was fixed before any score was seen, and neither was revised after seeing results. Nothing in colab/ was modified; scratch code is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cell/0f039315-b3a9-52ac-8187-9fae0d726994/scratchpad/wf/dmg_arm/run.py with per-pair scores saved as scores_*.npy alongside it. Note the shared scratchpad/wf/ directory is in concurrent use by another arm — a stale inspect.py there shadowed the stdlib module and broke numpy imports mid-run, so I isolated everything under wf/dmg_arm/.

candidates.hypothesis: Gene dosage gates the knockdown response — the knocked-down gene's copy number in a line sets how much depletion an shRNA can actually achieve, and each landmark's copy number sets how far it can move — so relative (cross-line z-scored) copy number should predict the gene x line interaction; it does not.
candidates.coverage: 8 of 9 lines. HEPG2 has NO row in depmap/OmicsAbsoluteCNGene.csv at all (its ModelID ACH-000739 is a valid DepMap model and is in Model.csv, but absent from the absolute-CN matrix), so features() returned None for HEPG2 rather than imputing; HEPG2's 3,562 pairs are excluded from both arms. Covered: PC3 MCF7 VCAP A375 HA1E A549 HT29 HCC515 = 29,635 of 33,197 pairs. Landmarks: 915/978 found in the CN table (63 missing set to 0, same convention as H.expression_baseline). Knocked-down genes: 3,465/3,801 found; the remaining 336 genes (2,609 of the 29,635 scored pairs) got gene-CN z = 0, again mirroring the baseline's fallback. Cross-line CN variance is real, not degenerate: median sd across the 8 lines is 0.78 copies, and only 0.1% of landmarks have sd < 0.05.
candidates.notes:
NUMBERS, same session, 3 H.evaluate runs at max_train_per_line=300, no tuning. (1) CN arm on the 8 CN-covered lines: -0.00082 (n=29,635). (2) H.expression_baseline on the SAME 8 lines and the same 29,635 pairs in the same order — the like-for-like reference reported above: +0.00573. (3) H.expression_baseline on all 9 lines: +0.00331 (n=33,197), which reproduces the documented 0.0029 and confirms the harness ran normally. Paired arm-minus-baseline: mu=-0.00655, se=0.00070, t=-9.36. Arm vs zero: mu=-0.00082, se=0.00025, t=-3.28 — i.e. indistinguishable from zero in effect size, if anything a hair below it. Construct ceiling 0.2487. Per held-out line the arm is negative in 6 of 8 (PC3 -0.0024, A549 -0.0021, HCC515 -0.0015, HT29 -0.0011, VCAP -0.0009, A375 -0.0007) and barely positive in 2 (MCF7 +0.0020, HA1E +0.0002); no line shows signal.

WHY IT IS ZERO, not just that it is. I measured the raw, unfitted quantity underneath the ridge: the correlation between a line's landmark CN-z profile and the residual, per pair. Mean signed r = +0.00138, mean |r| = 0.0341 across all 29,635 pairs. The noise floor for correlating two unrelated 978-dim vectors is 1/sqrt(978) = 0.032. So the landmark copy-number profile is essentially orthogonal to the interaction residual — there is nothing there for the ridge to find, and the slight negativity of the fitted arm is the sign coefficient learned on training lines failing to transfer to a held-out line.

STRUCTURAL CAVEAT that bounds this whole feature family. With the prescribed k=3 design (landmark vector, knocked-down-gene scalar, product), the prediction is p = lm*(b0 + b2*gz) + (b1*gz + b3). The additive term is constant across landmarks and drops out of a correlation, so the per-pair score is exactly +/- corr(lm, R): the predicted pattern is ALWAYS the same per-line CN profile, with only its SIGN varying by knocked-down gene. This arm therefore cannot express any gene-specific pattern, and its oracle-sign upper bound is mean|r| = 0.034 — 7x below the 0.2487 ceiling even before fitting. This limitation is identical in H.expression_baseline (same k=3 shape), so the head-to-head comparison is fair, but it means this is a test of "does relative dosage carry a per-line direction", not a general test of copy number. A gene-specific CN construct (e.g. CN of the landmark's known regulators) is untested and is not ruled out by this result.

CONFOUND WORTH FLAGGING: HA1E is a near-diploid immortalized normal kidney line, not a cancer line, so it contributes little CN variance; excluding it does not change the conclusion (the other 7 lines are also null).

candidates.hypothesis: Cell-line identity per se does not carry the interaction: under leave-one-line-out the held-out line's own one-hot is unidentifiable by construction, and the only thing that can transfer — shared OncotreeLineage — buys a gene-independent profile offset that is oracle-capped at ~0.021, because the residuals share a dominant profile axis whose sign along that axis is set by the gene, not the line.
candidates.coverage: Complete. All 9/9 lines (PC3 MCF7 VCAP A375 HA1E A549 HT29 HEPG2 HCC515) resolve to a DepMap ModelID via lincs/line_map.json and have an OncotreeLineage in Model.csv — nothing imputed. Lineages: Prostate {PC3, VCAP}, Lung {A549, HCC515}, Breast {MCF7}, Skin {A375}, Kidney {HA1E}, Bowel {HT29}, Liver {HEPG2} — i.e. only 4/9 lines have a same-lineage partner in the training set; 5/9 are lineage singletons. Features are gene-agnostic, so all 33,197/33,197 held-out (gene,line) pairs and all 3,801/3,801 genes were scored, same as the baseline arm (33,197). k=136 columns.
candidates.notes:
RUN: 2 H.evaluate calls, max_train_per_line=300, same process, same H.load(). Baseline H.expression_baseline = +0.003315 (n=33,197); arm = -0.012489 (median -0.0173, 47.8% of pairs positive). Paired delta -0.01580, se 0.00164, t = -9.64 — the arm is significantly WORSE than expression context and significantly below zero.

WHY THE SIGN IS NEGATIVE, NOT ZERO (matters for other arms). Two structural facts, both verified:
(1) The held-out line's one-hot column is identically zero in the training design, so the harness's ridge sets its coefficient to EXACTLY zero (A[j,j]=lam*n, all off-diagonals and A^T y entry zero; checked numerically = 0.0). Line identity therefore contributes literally nothing out-of-sample. This arm is in practice a test of lineage identity plus a line-independent global-shape term.
(2) That line-independent term is forced negative by leave-one-out arithmetic. With d_l = P[g,l] - mean_{l'!=l} P[g,l'], sum_l d_l = 0, so the average pattern over the 8 training lines equals -(1/8) x the held-out line's pattern. Any feature block that is constant across lines is fitted to that average and therefore predicts the held-out residual with the wrong sign. The correct null for a line-constant feature block under this protocol is a small NEGATIVE correlation, not zero. Consistent with this, all 5 lineage-singleton lines (where both one-hot blocks are dead) are negative: MCF7 -0.033, A375 -0.016, HA1E -0.051, HT29 -0.019, HEPG2 -0.021.

THE REFERENCE POINT ASKED FOR. Oracle upper bound for this whole family, computed directly on the held-out line (mean_g corr(d,R_g) is maximised at ||mean_g Rhat_g||): the best possible single gene-independent profile per line scores 0.0206 averaged over the 9 lines (0.016-0.026 per line). So even an oracle-fitted line-identity model reaches ~8% of the 0.2487 construct ceiling, and 0% of it is gene-specific. The gene-independent component carries ~1e-5 of the residual variance. Line identity alone bounds essentially nothing — mechanistic explanations are not competing with it.

WHERE THE INTERACTION ACTUALLY IS. If a per-gene coefficient is allowed along the top shared axis, an oracle 2-D span scores 0.412. So the residuals DO share a dominant profile axis that is a line property; what line identity cannot supply is the sign and magnitude each gene takes along it. That gene-specific loading is the interaction, and it is where a mechanistic arm has to bite.

ONE POSITIVE SIGNAL, REPORTED AS-IS. Lineage-shared lines average +0.0072 vs -0.0283 for singletons, but this is driven entirely by prostate: VCAP +0.046 and PC3 +0.022 (both above the 0.0033 baseline), while the other lineage pair, lung, is negative (A549 -0.022, HCC515 -0.019). n=2 lineage pairs, 1 of 2 transfers — not a general lineage effect. VCAP's +0.046 exceeds its own gene-independent oracle (0.0183), which is only possible because I included a rank-1 per-gene modulation (a coarse per-gene response-strength scalar s(g), computed excluding the line being featurized so it cannot transduce the held-out line's own profile) making the prediction u + s(g)*v rather than a fixed profile. So the arm is marginally MORE than pure line identity, and the honest reading of prostate is "lineage x gene-response-magnitude, rank one", not "line identity".
